main_text.l: qui inter Philosophos constat, morbum nihil
noctem diei, nam corpus terrę soli oppositum
umbram efficit. Cicero ipse in Topicis Sa-
inter aduersorum exempla posuit. At Boëtius
homo acutissimus, & in hoc disciplinæ genere
bonitatis. sic multi inter aduersorum exempla
tatem: cùm tamen à Physicis, disputetur fri-

modi, ut quædam tertium, siue me-

page.notes: The first word of the chapter is set with a large initial, read here as "VAE". The printed "V AE" may be a spacing artefact. The marks "?" after "diuisio" and "noctem" are printed question marks, not doubt marks. The long s is rendered as s throughout, and "funt" is read as "sunt". Reading "siccitatem" is based on the printed "ficcitatem", where the initial letter is a long s. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot.
